To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have obtained approximate solutions for the steady state diffusion equations for a self regulated system of two signalling molecules in a spherical cell.
the speed of signal propagation in the cytosplasm is a function of the number and the type of links in the signalling pathway.

the speed of signal transduction in the cell is an increasing function in the number of links of the cascade reaction and the speed of signal is a decreasing function of the diffusion coefficient of the signalling molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical analysis of cell signalling and the role of spatial effects in the process.
the mathematical analysis of cell signalling and the development of a model which describes the propagation of the intracellular signal.
understanding how signalling pathways are organized within the cell and how they are regulated by the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the speed of a signal is an increasing linear function of the number links in the cascade and the number of activating enzymes.
the speed of signal propagation is a monotonically increasing function of the length of the cascade, which is consistent with our previous results for a one-dimensional model.
the speed of signal transmission is an increasing function both of the number of compartments in a cell and of the number of signalling molecules in a cascade reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our work provides an analytical model for cell signalling in 3D and that the speed of signalling is an increasing function in the number of links.
the speed of signal transduction increases with the number of links of the cascade and the number of compartments.

we have developed a model of cell signal transductions which has a self regulated dynamic system and we have obtained approximate solutions to the diffusion equation for the signalling molecules and have investigated the speed of the propagation of the signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the speed of a signal is not necessarily a function of the diffusion coefficient alone.
the signal speed depends on the number of links and the number of links is a measure of complexity of the signal transduction system.
we can obtain approximate analytical solutions of the steady-state diffusion equation in a three-dimensional space.
